name: Naturalización (Carta de Naturaleza)

requirements.blocker_text: Requires 5 continuous years of domicile in Colombia, counted from the date the Resident (R) visa was issued.
requirements.fix_path: Hold Resident visa status continuously for 5 years.

requirements.blocker_text: Requires a clean criminal record, and a formal memorial (application letter) requesting Colombian nationality; the Ministry may conduct home visits to verify residence.

requirement_groups.name: Reduced-period track (spouse/permanent partner of a Colombian; parent of Colombian children; Spanish nationals)

requirements.blocker_text: Requires only 2 continuous years of domicile for: those married to or in a permanent partnership with a Colombian national; those with Colombian children; or Spanish nationals.
requirements.fix_path: Hold Resident visa status continuously for 2 years while in one of the qualifying categories.

requirements.blocker_text: Same clean-criminal-record and formal-memorial requirements as the ordinary track.

requirement_groups.name: Latin American / Caribbean nationals (reciprocity-based, per Ley 43 de 1993)

requirements.blocker_text: Ley 43 de 1993, Article 5, states Latin American and Caribbean nationals may naturalise after only 1 continuous year of domicile, subject to a reciprocity principle (i.e. Colombia's own nationals must receive equivalent treatment from that country). This reduced track was NOT mentioned on Cancillería's own current naturalización FAQ page (which cites only the 5-year, 2-year-spouse, 2-year-Colombian-children, and 2-year-Spanish-national tracks) -- it may have been narrowed, conditioned, or superseded by later regulation since 1993, or simply omitted from a simplified public FAQ. Not confirmed current in this pass.

evidence_required.document: Active Resident (R) visa, as principal or beneficiary
Foreign identity card and biographical passport page
Apostilled/legalized birth certificate with Spanish translation
Employment verification (labor certificate, RUT, or chamber-of-commerce registration)
Spanish language and constitutional-knowledge assessment (per Ley 43 Article 9)

sources.title: Cancillería de Colombia -- Naturalización: 5-year ordinary track, 2-year reduced track (spouse/Colombian-children/Spanish nationals), documents

Ley 43 de 1993 (Colombia's Nationality Law), hosted by ACNUR/UNHCR -- Article 5 (residence tracks including a 1-year Latin American/Caribbean reciprocity track), Article 9 (language/civics/character requirements)

notes: NEW ROUTE, part of Colombia's initial build. STATUS SET TO DRAFT: an unresolved discrepancy exists between Cancillería's current public FAQ page (tier-1, which lists only 5-year/2-year tracks) and the still-in-force 1993 Nationality Law (Ley 43, tier-2 as hosted by UNHCR though it is itself primary legislation) which additionally specifies a 1-year reciprocity-based track for Latin American/Caribbean nationals -- this was NOT re-confirmed at tier-1 in this pass, so rather than silently pick one source over the other, both are cited honestly and the whole route is held at draft pending reconciliation. THREE GENUINELY DIFFERENT RESIDENCE-LENGTH TRACKS (5yr/2yr/1yr) modelled as OR-logic groups for the same naturalisation process, following the same approach used for Greece's build -- Cancillería presents the 5-year and 2-year tracks as one unified process with alternative grounds, and the 1-year track (if still valid) would be a further alternative ground within that same process rather than a separate legal mechanism. required_prior_route_ids notes that Colombia's naturalisation clock runs from R-VISA issuance specifically, not M-visa time -- meaning the realistic TOTAL time to citizenship via the ordinary M-then-R-then-naturalisation chain can be as long as 5 (M, tiempo acumulado) + 5 (R, naturalización) = 10 years for someone with no family/nationality-based reduction, a materially longer combined timeline than either step suggests in isolation; flagged explicitly rather than left implicit.
